findings.question: q-chemistry-history-of-the-atom-0010
findings.quote: Modern atomic structure uses quantum states and orbitals. An orbital describes an electron’s state and spatial probability distribution.
findings.problem: The explanation uses undefined phrases such as “quantum states” and “spatial probability distribution.” A Grade 5 reader can select the correct choice yet still not understand what an orbital means.
findings.fix: Use plain English: “The modern model uses orbitals. An orbital shows where an electron is likely to be found around the nucleus.”

findings.question: q-chemistry-history-of-the-atom-0018
findings.quote: It is based on quantum states rather than a literal cloud of material.
findings.problem: The explanation discusses the literal-material misconception used in a wrong choice. The requested explanation rule permits only an explanation of the correct answer.
findings.fix: Replace with: “Darker parts of the picture show where an electron is more likely to be found.” Keep discussion of the literal-material mistake in its wrong-choice note.
